unusual_experiment.reason: Trigger identity available to this organ is minute-precision only and has no immutable shared request/turn id. Deterministic regressions below are ordinary validation, not the globally limited unusual experiment.

finding.claim: The autonomous terminal dispatch namespace had two provenance/transport weaknesses: rejected reserved markers could fall through as human UserPromptSubmit, and the final tmux autonomy sender accepted arbitrary printable text instead of only the one-shot token it claimed to carry.
finding.mechanism: consume_dispatch_prompt historically returned None for malformed, missing/replayed, wrong-nonce and expired reserved markers; terminal_hooks.user_prompt interprets None as the human path. Separately, TerminalSessionManager.dispatch_autonomy_prompt accepted arbitrary printable ASCII up to 256 chars. Together these leave an avoidable path for synthetic input to be misclassified or injected outside the exact dispatch-token contract.
evidence: Five direct consume-side namespace cases passed in an isolated source slice: ordinary non-prefixed, malformed, missing/replay, wrong nonce and expired.
Seven final-transport decision cases passed in an isolated source slice: one exact token admitted and six malformed/non-token forms rejected before tmux.
The hook/pulse source regression requires malformed/wrong/expired/replayed markers to create zero new canonical turn/workspace/causal artifacts and zero human-roundtrip attestation credit.
The terminal transport source regression requires only exact DISPATCH_PREFIX + 32 lowercase hex to reach tmux send-keys.
GitHub Actions runs 32493070380/96805028454 and 32493928244/96807778324 both ended before any visible step; zero pytest/runtime credit and no ClayVerse semantic failure.
Authorized Daytona plugin discovery in this interface returned no installable plugin; VPS/self-hosted/production testing was not used.

strongest_counterhypotheses: A rejected reserved marker is harmless because no stored autonomy instruction is exposed.
Consume-side fail-closed handling is sufficient, so constraining the tmux sender duplicates policy and adds no safety.
hypofusion.assessment: Both are rejected at their respective boundaries. The first misses provenance poisoning: synthetic-as-human classification itself is the defect. The second misses defense-in-depth at the final synthetic-input surface: a method documented as one-shot-token transport should not be a generic printable-text injector. A residual packaged-runtime hypothesis remains that Claude hook transport may transform the token before parser entry.
hypofusion.falsifier: Run exact private full-checkout dispatch + terminal transport + terminal hook + pulse adjacency. Inject malformed, wrong, expired and replayed markers; require zero canonical human artifacts/attestation. Exercise the final tmux sender with arbitrary printable text; require rejection before send-keys. Then repeat the accepted/rejected token path through the packaged managed Claude hook transport.
